name: Clean Water Montgomery Grant Program
summary: Montgomery County, Maryland grants for nonprofit-led watershed outreach, stewardship, restoration, tree planting, water quality monitoring and litter reduction projects.

geography.label: Montgomery County, Maryland outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg and Takoma Park

fiscal_sponsor.note: The sponsor applies and holds the money, for an organisation without 501(c)(3) status

eligibility.rule: Has current 501(c)(3) status or applies through a fiscal sponsor
If based outside Montgomery County, partners with a county community or a documented local partner
Does not request annual giving, fundraising, venture capital, lobbying, retroactive costs or traditional marketing
For Track 2, runs a voluntary project
For Track 2, keeps the project outside rights of way, easements and floodplains
For Track 2, keeps the project off government-owned or leased property
Completes the project within 18 months, or 24 months for water quality monitoring

documents: Track 2 proposed project design, if designs are not completed
Track 2 scaled planting plan and detailed plant list, if designs are completed
Track 2 landowner permission letter, if the applicant does not own the property
Track 2 detailed maintenance plan, if designs are completed

status.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Friday, November 13, 2026 at 4PM ET

deadline.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Friday, November 13, 2026 at 4PM ET

applicant_types.quote: Who can apply: Non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status, such as local watershed groups, faith-based organizations, service and civic groups, and more.

geography.quote: Implementation project location: Montgomery County, Maryland outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park.

access.quote: Start a New Application Click the button below to access and learn how to navigate our New Portal System

window.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Friday, November 13, 2026 at 4PM ET

amount.quote: Community Based Restoration projects up to $100,000

co_finance_required.quote: Match is encouraged but is not required.

fiscal_sponsor.quote: applicants must have a current tax-exempt 501(c)3 status. If your organization does not have a current 501(c)3 status, a fiscal sponsor may apply and secure funds on your behalf.

effort.quote: Applicants must submit applications in the Chesapeake Bay Trust Online System by 4:00 PM EST on 11/13/2026.

Each application is reviewed by a Technical Review Committee (TRC), composed of individuals who are experts in the fields supported by this RFP and represent communities engaged by projects funded by this RFP.

eligibility.quote: applicants must have a current tax-exempt 501(c)3 status. If your organization does not have a current 501(c)3 status, a fiscal sponsor may apply and secure funds on your behalf.

Applicants not based in Montgomery County must demonstrate partnership with a Montgomery County community or have a Montgomery-based partner whose role is clearly articulated in the application and in a Letter of Commitment from that partner.

• Annual giving, fundraising, and/or venture capital; • Political lobbying; • Reimbursement for a project that has been completed or materials that have already been purchased; • Traditional marketing
Landowner permission is required for all projects;
Projects cannot be located within a right of way, easement, or floodplain.
Projects cannot be located on County, State, or Federal owned or leased properties, including land owned by the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC);

Projects must be completed within 18 months upon receipt of the award. Water Quality Monitoring projects may request up to 24 months, to allow sufficient time for seasonal water quality monitoring activities.

after_award.quote: If approved, the Trust will send an award agreement with award conditions and due dates of status, progress, and final reports.
Additionally, Montgomery County shall be allowed access to the site to assess and support the function of the restoration practice in perpetuity;

documents.quote: Have you included a list of your knowledge objectives that tell us what participants will learn from your project? Evaluation plan: Have you included methods of evaluation in knowledge for project participants, such as drafts of pre- and post-surveys?

Proposed project design: Have you provided a plan view or site/concept plan, if designs are not completed? *Note: If awarded, a final, completed site plan must be submitted to the Trust for approval prior to any installation work. Planting Plans: If designs are completed, have you provided a scaled planting plan and a detailed plant list?
Landowner permission: Did you include a letter from the property owner stating approval to implement the project at the site for projects implemented on property not owned by the applicant?

Detailed maintenance plan: If designs are completed, did you include a detailed, draft maintenance plan signed by the entity responsible for maintenance and the landowner (if different than organization applying)?
Monitoring Sites: Have you included a list of proposed monitoring sites?
Proposed location(s) of litter clean ups: Have you provided the proposed locations of the litter clean ups?
